technical_body.purpose: Per-call billing record generated by the originating CO switch. Captures calling number, called number, start/end timestamps, trunk group used, call type, and completion status.
technical_body.hardware_era_pre_ss7: Paper tape (early), then magnetic tape (BSTJ 1958), then online AMATPS tape drives. Physical tapes were transported to a Regional Accounting Office for reconciliation.
technical_body.hardware_era_ss7: Digital streams over BX.25/OSI, later over IP.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: The primary billing evidence a phreak wanted to defeat. Blue-boxing produced misaligned AMA (see technique_blue_box_domestic vulnerability_window); tandem stacking produced AMA on each tandem that didn't tie to any billed customer.
technical_body.died_because: Not dead — modernized to CDR streams on packet-switched core, but the same concept.

technical_body.purpose: A predecessor / variant of AMA where multiple small COs sent their raw call data to a central accounting office for batch processing rather than generating complete AMA locally.
technical_body.typical_deployment: Small step-by-step and crossbar offices that lacked SPC intelligence to generate their own AMA. CAMA-enabled trunks carried ANI + called number to the CAMA center.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: CAMA trunks were vulnerable to ANI spoofing — a phreak with MF pulsing capability could send fake ANI to a CAMA center, misattributing the call.
technical_body.died_because: Replaced by SPC-generated AMA as small offices upgraded to 5ESS/DMS-100.

technical_body.purpose: AT&T Long Lines program that logged unusual 2600 Hz hold-time patterns on interoffice trunks. Detected blue-box seizure attempts before the far-end tandem committed to the reroute.

detection_mechanism.2600_hold_alarm: A tone burst held for >~400 ms triggered a suspect-call record on 1AESS generic 1AE7+ and 4ESS.
detection_mechanism.MF_after_2600_pattern: Post-2600 MF pulses that didn't originate from a normal operator/tandem position were flagged.

technical_body.response_to_hits: Suspect calls were logged and reviewed. Repeated hits on a single originating line escalated to AT&T Security -> USSS referral (Bernie S 1995 case, etc.).
technical_body.phreak_relevance: Every serious blue-box attempt after ~1975 was already being logged. Greenstar/blueflag is *why* the blue-box scene shifted from bulk fraud to short-hop exploration by the 1980s.
technical_body.died_because: Superseded by SS7's inherent out-of-band signaling — 2600 Hz on the voice path no longer means anything for supervision, so there is nothing to log.

technical_body.shipped_in: 1AESS generic 1AE7 and later, 4ESS from initial deployment
technical_body.meaning: The switch fires an alarm when 2600 Hz is detected in the voice path for longer than ~400 ms after answer supervision. Normal call teardown produced a shorter tone burst; blue-box seizure required a longer hold to trigger the far-end tandem's wink.
technical_body.notes: The threshold varied by switch generation and by generic-load version. Community lore about '750-1000 ms is safe' is a reaction to this alarm — phreaks who held tone too long got flagged, so the community moved to shorter, sharper bursts.
technical_body.false_positives: Occasional legitimate DTMF-in-2600-Hz-band harmonics, subscriber whistling into the mouthpiece, etc. Most were filtered by requiring MF pulses to follow within a short window.

technical_body.purpose: Bell operating support system for tracking loop-plant trouble tickets. When a subscriber called repair (611), the ticket went into LMOS; craft technicians dispatched from LMOS work queues.
phreak_relevance: LMOS was itself dial-up accessible from craft terminals — a phreak-accessible entry to LEC internals.
Phrack 9.9 and 18.8 both documented LMOS command sets.
LMOS records could reveal what testing was being done on a target loop — including whether the phreak's own loop was under active fault investigation.
technical_body.died_because: Consolidated into Telcordia OSS-J and later carrier-specific ticketing systems in the 2000s.

name: COSMOS — COmputer System for Mainframe OperationS

technical_body.purpose: Bell operating support system for managing frame-based switch cross-connects. Tracks which physical wire pair terminates on which piece of switch equipment (line equipment number / LEN <-> DN mapping).
phreak_relevance: Extensively documented in Phrack 26.5, 27.5, 31.6 (Erik Bloodaxe's 'Definitive COSMOS').

Access to COSMOS meant you could look up any subscriber's physical wire assignment — which pair on which frame in which CO — enabling physical-access attacks (beige-boxing at the correct terminal block).
Also could reveal test numbers and unassigned equipment that a phreak could then have activated.
technical_body.died_because: Absorbed into TIRKS and later Telcordia OSS. By the 2000s the Bell OSS landscape was fragmented across many post-divestiture successors.

technical_body.purpose: Bell OSS that provisioned the memory-resident translations on SPC switches (1ESS, 1AESS). Downloaded translation tables into the switch's memory store; roughly the tool an admin used to program what phone numbers routed where.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: Access to MIZAR was rare and highly-privileged. Successful compromise let a phreak alter translations on live 1ESS/1AESS switches without being at the RCV/TTY console.

technical_body.purpose: CO switch feature that logs the calling party's identity for every call to a subscribed target DN. Available as a subscriber feature (customer opts in and gets a monthly report) or as a police-request LEA feature.
technical_body.typical_activation: Subscriber presses *57 after an offending call, or LEA arranges via the switch's craft interface.
technical_body.phreak_relevance_defender: MCT is what defenders enable on likely-abused DNs (DISA numbers, VMB access, ANAC). Attackers must check whether MCT is active before targeting a DN.
technical_body.phreak_relevance_meridian: On Meridian PBXs, LD 51 is the MCT overlay. LD 22 PRT PKG reveals whether pkg 107 (MCT) is licensed.

technical_body.purpose: Bell system for remote monitoring of switching equipment. Used by CO craft and security to bridge into calls silently (busy-verify + emergency-interrupt from a remote terminal, not from a physically-present TSPS operator).
technical_body.phreak_relevance: The mythical 'wiretap' capability the FBI-of-lore was rumored to have — REMOBS was closer to real than most conspiracy theories credited. Documented in Phrack 14.4 (Taran King).
technical_body.died_because: Absorbed into modern CALEA-mandated lawful-intercept subsystems on 5ESS/DMS/EWSD.

technical_body.purpose: Fraud-detection systems that ingest SS7 signaling records and CDR streams in near-real-time, looking for patterns: sudden long-distance minute spikes on a single line, calls to known premium-rate destinations, unusual international-call frequency.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: A DISA-abused PBX makes many long-duration international calls in a short time window. Fraud analytics catch this pattern within minutes on well-monitored networks, so modern DISA fraud requires either a target with no analytics (small hotel, abandoned box) or short bursts under the detection window.
